raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. Sixty-nine years old now, knees aren't what they were, but I know this soil. My son is working in Shijiazhuang — he sends money sometimes — so it's mostly me and my wife.

I'll do what I've always done: **winter wheat, then summer maize**. That's the rotation here. My father did it, I do it. Ten mu of land. I could contract some of it out to the village cooperative, but then what would I do all day? And I still need grain for the house.

For wheat, I'll use the Jimai variety I've been buying from the township supply station for years. It doesn't fail me. I'll rotary-till after the maize harvest in October, broadcast the base fertilizer — urea and diammonium phosphate mixed in — then drill the seed. Four irrigations: the winter water before freezing, jointing, heading, and grain fill. I know the well schedule. Spray once for weeds in the winter rosette stage, once more for aphids and rust in April. That's enough.

For maize after wheat, I'll direct-seed — no ploughing, just plant straight into the stubble. My neighbor has a seeder. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958, I've used it for fifteen years. Two topdress nitrogen applications. Rain is usually decent in July and August, but I'll pump once if it gets dry. One herbicide spray early, one for borer if I see the moths.

I won't try anything new this year. At my age, a bad experiment costs more than it's worth.
